title: Section pullbacks of left fibrations model coherent homotopy fibers
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, coherent functor categories and homotopy fibers of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and space-valued transport of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Fix a universe containing a small simplicial set $B$, left fibrations $p:X\to B$, $p':X'\to B$, and a simplicial map $f:X\to X'$ satisfying $p'f=p$. Suppose that $f$ itself is a left fibration of simplicial sets. Let $s:B\to X'$ be a section of $p'$, and form the degreewise pullback $Y=B\times_{s,X',f}X$. Then $Y\to B$ is a left fibration. Under space-valued transport, let $G,G':B\to\mathcal S$ classify $p,p'$, and let $a:G\to G'$ and $b:1_B\to G'$ correspond to $f,s$, where $1_B$ is the constant terminal-space functor. The coherent functor classifying $Y\to B$, together with its projection to $G$, is naturally equivalent to
$$G\mathop{\times}^{h}_{G'}1_B$$
in $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S)$, with maps $a,b$. Here the homotopy pullback is the limit of the span and is computed pointwise: at each vertex $t$, it is the space of $x\in G(t)$ and a path from $a_t(x)$ to $b_t(*)$, including all higher simplices. This identification matches the actual pullback projections, is natural under restriction of $B$, and therefore identifies induced coherent cocones, not merely their apex objects.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2 (covariant dual), Lemma 2.1.3.3 for the fiber maps being Kan fibrations, and the homotopy-pullback assertion in the proof of Lemma 5.5.4.13, printed pp. 479-480. The natural section-pullback formulation is the generic left-fibration calculus underlying that argument. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: Let $q:Y\to B$ and $r:Y\to X$ be the actual pullback projections. Thus $fr=sq$ and $pr=q$. Check the lifting property directly using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Given a left-horn lifting problem for $q$, with lower simplex $v:\Delta^n\to B$ and upper horn $h:\Lambda_i^n\to Y$, use the horn $rh$ and the lower simplex $sv$ to lift against $f$. The resulting $w:\Delta^n\to X$ satisfies $fw=sv$, so $(v,w)$ is a simplex of $Y$ extending $h$. Consequently $q$ is a left fibration. The same argument shows that a pullback of any left fibration has the left-horn lifting property; we use this below for vertex fibers. Only the assumed lifting property of $f$, not any fibrancy of $B$, was used.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, proof, displayed pullback Y on printed pp.479-480; base change of the horn lifting property

proof.text: Fix a vertex $t:\Delta^0\to B$. The strict fibers $X_t,X'_t$ are left fibrations over $\Delta^0$ by the pullback argument in step 1 and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. We obtain their full Kan properties from [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber], rather than assuming that left horns include all horns. Explicitly, for a simplicial set $K$ let $(K^{\mathrm{op}})_n=K_n$, with faces $d_i^{\mathrm{op}}=d_{n-i}$ and degeneracies $s_i^{\mathrm{op}}=s_{n-i}$ in degree $n$. Reversal carries $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, and hence exchanges left and right lifting properties and preserves the all-horn property. Apply the cited right-fibration theorem to $X_t^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta^0$ and $(X'_t)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta^0$, whose bases are Kan. Reversing back proves that $X_t,X'_t$ are Kan. Next $f_t:X_t\to X'_t$ is the pullback of $f$ along $X'_t\to X'$, hence a left fibration. Apply the same theorem to $f_t^{\mathrm{op}}$, now over the Kan complex $(X'_t)^{\mathrm{op}}$, and reverse its all-horn lifts. Thus $f_t$ is a Kan fibration. Empty fibers are allowed throughout.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.3.3, printed p.66; its right-handed counterpart is Kerodon Corollary 4.4.3.8 (01NV), used through the existing right-fibration-space-fiber node

proof.text:
The degreewise pullback formula of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] identifies $Y_t$ exactly with $X_t\times_{X'_t}\Delta^0$, where the second map is the vertex $s_t$. Put
$$P_t=X_t\times_{X'_t,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X'_t)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,X'_t}\Delta^0.$$
All three input spaces are Kan and $f_t$ is a Kan fibration by step 2. Therefore [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] gives the weak homotopy equivalence $Y_t\to P_t$ inserting the constant path at $f_t(x)=s_t(*)$. This is the comparison of the actual cones: its maps to $X_t$ and $\Delta^0$ are the original projections, and its path is their specified constant commutation path. By the homotopy-pullback model clause of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], this strict pullback is the model-categorical homotopy pullback of the Kan cospan $X_t\xrightarrow{f_t}X'_t\xleftarrow{s_t}\Delta^0$, since the leg $f_t$ already is a fibration and requires no replacement. To pass to the infinity category $\mathcal S$ of spaces, apply the cospan clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams] to the Kan model structure on simplicial sets, in which every object is cofibrant and $X_t,X'_t,\Delta^0$ are fibrant, with the path object $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X'_t)$: the strict pullback $P_t$, with its induced cone (the two projections and the evaluated path as commutation homotopy), represents the pullback of this cospan in $\mathcal S$. The weak homotopy equivalence $Y_t\to P_t$ commutes strictly with the projections to $X_t$ and $\Delta^0$, and pulls the path homotopy back to the constant one; hence the strict cone of $Y_t$ is the restriction of the limiting cone of $P_t$ along an equivalence of apices, and is itself limiting in $\mathcal S$. The displayed $P_t$ retains the entire simplicial path, not only a component or a point.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7 (Kerodon 0329), path model Construction 3.4.0.3 (010B); Kan-model homotopy-pullback interpretation supplied by the cited node

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] to the entire strictly commuting square $(Y,X,B,X')$ over $B$, retaining both projections and its equality $fr=sq$. A constant terminal-space functor is represented by $B\to B$, so its image is a coherent cone from the classifying functor $H$ of $q$ to the span $G\xrightarrow{a}G'\xleftarrow{b}1_B$. The classification is coherent in maps, composition and base pullback. Consequently, evaluation at $t$ identifies this cone, including its commutation homotopy, with the strict fiber cone of step 3, up to an equivalence of cones. In particular, this is not a choice of an unrelated equivalence $H(t)\simeq P_t$: the comparison comes from $r,q$ and the equality just specified. A cone's universal mapping-space condition is unchanged by such an equivalence, since the corresponding test-map spaces and their cone maps are identified by equivalences. Each evaluated cone is therefore limiting. Now apply the general small-simplicial-set, objectwise-limit clause of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] with $K=B$, $\mathcal V=\mathcal S$ and the finite cospan shape. Its hypothesis on the existence of the corresponding limits in $\mathcal S$ holds: the same cited node states that spaces admit all small limits. This proves that this very cone with apex $H$ is limiting in $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S)$. Thus it realizes $G\times^h_{G'}1_B$, with the actual projection to $G$. Step 3 supplies its asserted pointwise path description.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.3, printed p.319, with opposites for limits; Theorem 2.2.1.2 and the homotopy-pullback argument of Lemma 5.5.4.13

proof.text:
For any map $u:C\to B$ of small simplicial sets, degreewise pullback gives a canonical isomorphism
$$u^*Y\cong C\times_{u^*X'}u^*X,$$
with the section $u^*s$, and it commutes with both projections. The isomorphism simply forgets the repeated base coordinate, so its isomorphisms for composable base maps agree. The pulled-back comparison $u^*f$ is still a left fibration by step 1. Classification commutes coherently with these base pullbacks by [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Applying step 4 to $C$ therefore shows that the restricted cone is the limit of the restricted span. This also follows directly from the objectwise-limit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. The limiting cones are terminal objects of their coherent cone category, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; their full subcategory is a contractible Kan complex by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Hence the identification with any notation for the homotopy pullback is the equivalence of limiting cones, with its coherent compatibility, and respects the displayed restriction maps and their composites. The square was transported as a whole, and restriction keeps all its simplices. In particular, when $B$ itself carries a cone or cocone parameter, this identifies the induced coherent cones or cocones and their structure maps, including all higher compatibility simplices. No passage to apex objects alone occurs.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.3 and classification naturality; universal property and contractible space of limiting cones applied to the projection square
